info.title: Ambivo Messaging API
info.description:
**Messaging** is people writing to people inside Ambivo: one-to-one chats, group
rooms, attachments, read state, typing, and the push that wakes a phone. It
runs on two backends.

| Backend | Host | Who uses it | What it holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core chat** | `goferapi.ambivo.com` | CRM mobile app, Ambivo Chat app for people without encryption keys, the ambivo-nx Messages screens | Plain-text direct messages, rooms (group, team and client chats), attachments, contacts, the `/chat` WebSocket |
| **Encrypted chat service** | `chatapi.ambivo.com` | Ambivo Chat app and the CRM app's Chats tab, for people who have published device keys | Public keys and ciphertext only. It cannot read a message. |

Customer texting (SMS, MMS, fax) is documented in the **CRM** spec under SMS:
`/messages/send_sms`, `/phone/user/send_sms`, `/admin/send_sms`, `/bot/send_sms`.
A room message with `user_message_type: sms` is the one SMS path described here.

## Which backend a screen should use

The ambivo-nx Messages screens (side panel, full page, toast) read and search
message text, show the files shared in a chat and link CRM records. That needs a
server that can read messages, so they use **Core chat**: direct messages for
one-to-one chats and rooms for groups. The encrypted service cannot search,
preview a record or count unread messages for you; those live on the device.

Build those screens on the **Messages** routes (`/user/messaging/...`). They are
JSON with real verbs and cover the whole screen: the chat list with pinned chats
and unread counts, history around a found message, send with a reply or a linked
record, edit, delete that leaves a stub, reactions, read state ("seen" in a
group), mute, the files and records shared in a chat, and one search over every
chat. They read and write the same direct messages and rooms as the older routes,
so the mobile apps see the same chats.

**Host.** Call every Core chat route at `https://goferapi.ambivo.com`, from the web
app and the mobile apps. That keeps chat traffic off the servers that answer the
web app. Use the same login token you use everywhere else. The `/chat` WebSocket
is at `wss://socket.ambivo.com/chat`.

A conversation is `direct` (its id is the other person's user id) or `room` (its
id is the room id).

Every list on these routes follows the house standard: `page_num` and
`page_size` (skip = (page_num - 1) * page_size), `match_filter_dict` and
`sort_dict` as JSON query arguments, `search_text`, and `get_count=true` for the
count alone. Lists answer `total_count`, `page_num` and `page_size`. There are no
cursors.

| Screen | Route |
|---|---|
| Messages list, filters All / Unread / Chats / Groups, search people and chats | `GET /user/messaging/conversations?match_filter_dict=&search_text=` |
| Badge on the Messages icon | `GET /user/messaging/unread` |
| Open a chat; scroll up for more | `GET .../conversations/{kind}/{id}/messages?page_num=` |
| Send, reply, share the record I'm on, send a photo | `POST .../conversations/{kind}/{id}/messages` (upload first with `/messages/attachment_send`) |
| Mark as read when the chat is open | `POST .../conversations/{kind}/{id}/read` |
| React, edit, delete | `POST|DELETE /user/messaging/messages/{kind}/{id}/reactions`, `PATCH|DELETE /user/messaging/messages/{kind}/{id}` |
| Search messages; open a result at the message | `GET /user/messaging/search`, then the chat's messages with `anchor_message_id` |
| Find in this chat | `GET .../conversations/{kind}/{id}/messages?search_text=` |
| Details: members, files, linked records, mute, leave | `POST /room/info`, `GET .../files`, `GET .../records`, `PUT .../mute`, `POST /room/remove` |
| Pin a chat | `PUT .../conversations/{kind}/{id}/pin` |
| Resize the side panel; open it at the saved width | `PUT /user/messaging/settings` `{panel_width}`, read it with `GET /user/messaging/settings` |
| Start a new chat | One person: send to `direct/{user id}`. Two or more: `POST /room/manage` with `user_ids`, then send to the room. People search: `POST /user/directory/search`. |
| New-message toast, typing, live updates | the `/chat` WebSocket below |

## Core chat conventions

**Auth.** `Authorization: Bearer <login token>` on every route unless a route says
otherwise. A missing or expired token is HTTP **401 with an empty body**.

**Input.** Most Core chat routes are older handlers that read the **query string
or a form-encoded body** (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`). They ignore a JSON
body. Each operation says which it takes. A comma-separated value is a list
(`msgid=a,b,c`).

**Envelope.** HTTP 200 with `result`:

```json
{ "result": 1, "messages": [ ... ], "last_id": "65f0...", "current_timestamp": 1729800000 }
{ "result": 2, "error_code": "NOT_ROOM_ADMIN", "error": { "message": "..." } }
```

Older handlers build `error_code` from the error's sentence, for example
`INVALID_MSG_ID` or `INVALID_CHATTING_ROOM_ID__<id>` (the id is part of the
code). Match on the prefix. These carry `status_code` in the body.

**Ids and time.** Ids are 24-character hex strings. `date_time` and
`current_timestamp` are unix **seconds**. `timestamp` and `created_at` are the
stored date as a string.

**Paging.** Newest first. Pass the `last_id` from the previous page to get the
next, older page, with `page_size`.

## How Core stores a chat

There is no conversation record.

* A **direct chat** is every message between two people. Each message is stored
  twice: the sender's copy (`bin` 0) and the recipient's copy (`bin` 1). Each
  side reads, edits and deletes through its own copy's id. `user_msg_cnt` holds
  the unread count per pair.
* A **room** (`chatting_rooms`) has `members`, each with a `member_role`: `0`
  writer, `1` admin, `2` client. `room_type` is `regular`, `team` (staff only) or
  `client` (a customer and the staff who serve them, often over SMS).
* A **room message** (`room_messages`) is stored once. A reply in a thread has
  `parent_message_id` set to its root; a top-level message has `"-1"`.

Direct chat crosses tenants: anyone can write to anyone they can find, unless
that person blocked them. Rooms belong to one tenant.

## Who may manage a room

A **room admin** (`member_role` 1), an **admin of the tenant that owns the room**,
or an Ambivo super admin. Being admin of your own tenant gives nothing in another
tenant's room. Members may read, post, leave (when `allow_self_remove`), and join
on their own when the room has `allow_self_add`.

## Realtime: the `/chat` WebSocket

`wss://socket.ambivo.com/chat`. Not an OpenAPI operation, so the contract is here
and under `x-websockets`.

1. Sign in. Every login-shaped response carries `client_connection_id`.
2. Open the socket and send
   `{"type":"intro","sender_id":"<your user id>","connection_id":"<client_connection_id>"}`.
   The server checks that `connection_id` belongs to that user. A bad one gets
   `{"type":"error","error_code":"invalid_client_connection_id"}` and the socket
   stays unregistered. Never make a connection id up.
3. Frames that act as you (typing, editing) are dropped until the intro succeeds,
   and always carry your id as `sender_id`, whatever the client sends.

**You send**

| `type` | Fields | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `intro` | `sender_id`, `connection_id`, optional `device_id`, `os` | Registers the socket |
| `activity_typing` | `recipient_id` (or `to_id`) for a direct chat, or `room_id`; optional `typing: false` | The other person, or every other room member, gets `activity_typing` with your `sender_id` (and `room_id`). `typing: false` sends `activity_stop_typing`. |
| `activity_stop_typing` | same | Stop indicator |
| `subscribe_channel` / `unsubscribe_channel` | `channel_name` | Record list channels. Chat does not use channels. |
| `ping` | anything | Ignored. Sending something every 30 s keeps an idle socket open. |

**You receive**

| `type` | When | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | A direct message arrives | `sender_id`, `recipient_id`, `message` (text), `original_text`, `user_message_type`, `sender_nickname`, `avatar_url`, `recipient_msgid` (your copy's id), `sender_msgid`, `friend`, `ts`; with an attachment also `attachment_id`, `att_filename`, `att_filesize`, `att_url`, `thumbnail_url`, `content_type` |
| `message_read` | The other person read your message | `sender_id`, `recipient_id`, `message_id`, `mirror_msgid` |
| `message_edited` | A direct message you received was edited | `message_id` (your copy), `new_text` |
| `message_deleted` | A direct message you received was deleted | `message_id` (your copy) |
| `room_message` | Someone posted in a room you are in | `room_id`, `room_name`, `msgid`, `parent_message_id`, `sender_id`, `sender_name`, `message`, `user_message_type`, `unread_msg_cnt` (yours, from your read state; 0 until you first read the room), `avatar_url`, `room_avatar_url`, `room`, `ts` |
| `room_message_edited` | | `room_id`, `room_name`, `message_id`, `new_text` |
| `room_message_deleted` | | `room_id`, `room_name`, `message_id` |
| `added_to_room` | You were added | `room_id`, `room_name`, `sender_id`, `sender_nickname`, `room_details` |
| `removed_from_room` | You were removed | `room_id`, `room_name`, `user_id` |
| `activity_typing` / `activity_stop_typing` | Someone is typing to you | `sender_id`, `room_id` for a room |
| `user_presence_update` | A colleague's phone presence changed | `user_id`, `message.data.presence_status_dict` |
| `message_reaction` | Someone reacted to a direct message | `message_id` (your copy), `sender_id`, `reactions` |
| `room_message_reaction` | Someone reacted in a room | `room_id`, `message_id`, `sender_id`, `reactions` |
| `room_read` | A member read a room up to a message | `room_id`, `user_id`, `up_to_message_id` |

Messages sent with a reply or a record also carry `reply_to` and `record_ref` in
`message` and `room_message`. A delete through the Messages routes adds
`deleted: true` to `message_deleted` / `room_message_deleted`, and an edit adds
`edited_at` to the edited frames.

Nothing is queued for an offline socket. After a reconnect, read with
`/messages/fetch_recent_conversations` and the fetch routes.

## Push

A new message also pushes to the recipient's phones (Firebase), unless they muted
that sender or room or set their status to busy. The data payload `type` is
`N010` for a direct message (`id` = your copy's id, `sender_id`, `sender_msgid`,
`recipient_msgid`) and `N009` for a room message (`room_id`, `room_name`,
`parent_message_id`, `unread_msg_cnt`). Phones register for push with
`POST /user/device_registrations/manage`.

## Encrypted chat service

`https://chatapi.ambivo.com/v1/...`. The service stores public keys and opaque
ciphertext. Encryption runs on the phone (Signal protocol).

**Auth.** Mint a short-lived chat token from Core with
`POST /user/chat_token?device_id=<device>` using your login token. It lasts
3600 s (`aud` `ambivo-chat`). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <chat token>` and
send `X-Device-Id`. On 401, mint a new one and retry once. The service checks the
token against Core's `/.well-known/jwks.json`.

**Envelope.** The same `result` shape, with `request_path` on errors. HTTP status
varies: validation errors and `ROOM_NOT_FOUND` are 200; auth is 401;
`NOT_A_MEMBER` and `NOT_MESSAGE_OWNER` are 403; some routes use 400, 404, 502 or
503. Branch on `result` and `error_code`.

**Model.** A room has members. A message is one **envelope per recipient device**,
all sharing one `message_id`. Each device reads its own envelopes with
`GET /v1/sync` and keeps history locally; the server copy cannot be decrypted
twice. Delivered and read ticks are per envelope and add up to `sent`,
`delivered` or `read` per message for the sender.

**WebSocket.** `wss://chatapi.ambivo.com/v1/ws?token=<chat token>&device_id=<device>`.
A bad token fails the upgrade with HTTP 403. Frames use the key `t`:

| `t` | Direction | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `envelope` | in | The EncEnvelope schema. The server marks it delivered once forwarded. |
| `receipt` | in | `room_id`, `message_id`, `kind` (`delivered`/`read`), `status` (`sent`/`delivered`/`read`), `by_user_id`, `by_device_id`, `at`. Sent to the sending device. |
| `senderkey` | in | `room_id`, `epoch`, `sender_device_id`, `ciphertext` |
| `backup_available` | in | `user_id`, `updated_at`, `at` |
| `deleted` | in | `message_id`, `room_id`. The sender deleted it for everyone; drop the bubble. |
| `call_invite`, `call_accept`, `call_decline`, `call_cancel`, `call_end`, `call_busy` | both | `to_user_id`, `call_id`, `media` (`audio`/`video`), `channel`; the server adds `from_user_id`, `from_device_id`, `ts`. Relayed only to someone you share a room with. |
| `read` | out | `room_id`, `up_to_envelope_id` |
| `ack` | out | `message_ids` |

A connected device counts as online; the server refreshes it every 45 s, so a
phone with the socket open gets no push. Typing and presence are not on this
socket; the apps send typing on Core's `/chat` socket.

**Push.** For a device that is offline the service asks Core to push
`{type: "chat", room_id, message_id, sender_user_id}` with no message content, and
`{type: "call", call_id, channel, media, from_user_id, ts}` for a call.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description:
The JSON routes for the ambivo-nx Messages screens. One model over direct
chats and rooms: a conversation is `direct` (id = the other person) or `room`
(id = the room). Signed in and tenant approved on every route.

tags.name: Direct messages
tags.description: One-to-one chat on Core. Plain text, stored as a sender copy and a recipient copy.

tags.name: Rooms
tags.description: Group, team and client chats on Core. Creating, reading, members and roles.

tags.name: Room messages
tags.description: Posting, reading, editing, deleting and searching messages in a room. Threads use `parent_message_id`.

tags.name: Attachments
tags.description: Uploading a file for a chat and reading it back.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: People to chat with. The tenant directory, phone-book matching, friend requests and blocking.

tags.name: Realtime and push
tags.description: Chat tokens for the encrypted service, push registration, and call signalling over the socket.

tags.name: Encrypted: keys
tags.description: The public-key directory. Each device publishes an identity key, a signed prekey and one-time prekeys.

tags.name: Encrypted: rooms and messages
tags.description: Rooms, sending envelopes, catching up with sync, receipts, delete, sender keys.

tags.name: Encrypted: files and backup
tags.description: Encrypted attachments and the passphrase-encrypted chat backup, both through signed storage links.

tags.name: Encrypted: settings and tools
tags.description: Read-receipt setting, blocks, link previews, call tokens, push tokens and health.

tags.name: Encrypted: Telegram
tags.description: A tenant's Telegram bot inbox. These messages are not end-to-end encrypted.

core_chat.auth: intro frame with sender_id and the server-issued client_connection_id

encrypted_chat.auth: chat token in the query string; a bad token fails the upgrade with HTTP 403

get.description:
Your direct chats and rooms in one list. With no `sort_dict`, pinned chats come
first, then the newest. `unread_count` is per person and stops at 100; show
"99+" above 99. Someone who has never read a room since read state began counts
the messages they never opened, until their first read.

`match_filter_dict` keys: `kind` (`direct`|`room`), `unread` (`true`), `pinned`,
`muted` (booleans), `room_type` (`regular`|`team`|`client`). Any other key is
`INVALID_FILTER`. `sort_dict`: one of `last_activity_at`, `name`,
`unread_count`, with `1` or `-1` (`INVALID_SORT` otherwise). `search_text`
matches part of the name.

200.description: One page of the list, or `{total_count}` with get_count
Counts, each stopping at 100 per chat

get.description:
Settings for the Messages screens, saved per person on the server, so they
follow you to every browser and device. `panel_width` is the docked side panel
width in CSS pixels; `null` means you never saved one, so use the app default.

put.description:
Only the keys you send change. Send `null` to clear one. An unknown key, an
empty body, or a width that is not a whole number from 320 to 1600 is
`INVALID_BODY`, and nothing is saved. Save once when the drag ends, not on
every move.

200.description: All your settings after the change

get.description:
Messages containing `search_text` (any case, at least 2 characters,
`SEARCH_TOO_SHORT`) in every chat you are in. Newest first unless `sort_dict`
is `{"created_at": 1}`. The first 1,000 hits can be paged.

`match_filter_dict` keys: `kind` (`direct`|`room`), `conversation_id` (needs
`kind`), `sender_id`. To show a hit in its chat, read the chat's messages with
`anchor_message_id` set to the hit's `message_id`.

200.description: One page of hits, or `{total_count}` with get_count

get.description:
Paged by `page_num` / `page_size`, newest first unless `sort_dict` is
`{"created_at": 1}`. In a room, top-level messages only, unless
`match_filter_dict` names a `thread_id`.

`match_filter_dict` keys: `thread_id` (rooms), `sender_id`, `has_attachment`
(`true`). `search_text` keeps messages containing it (find in this chat).
`anchor_message_id` answers the page that holds that message, and the
response's `page_num` says which page that is (`MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND` if it is not
in this chat).

Deleted messages come back as stubs with `deleted: true` and no text. Your own
messages carry `seen` (direct) or `seen_by_count` (room). Records you may not
open come back with `record_card.available: false`.

200.description: One page of messages, or `{total_count}` with get_count

post.description:
Text, a file, a record, or any mix. Upload a file first with
`/messages/attachment_send` and send its `att_id` as `attachment_id`; it must be
your upload (`ATTACHMENT_NOT_FOUND`). A record is checked against your access (`RECORD_NOT_AVAILABLE`).
`reply_to_id` must be a message in this chat (`REPLY_NOT_IN_CHAT`).

Delivery is the same as the older send routes: the `message` or `room_message`
socket frame and a push. Sending in a room marks it read for you up to your
message. Refusals from the older routes pass through, for example
`INVALID_RECIPIENT` and `YOU_ARE_IN_BLACKLIST`.

value.text: Can you take this one? She asked for a call back after 3.

post.description:
Up to `up_to_message_id`, or everything so far. Never moves back. In a direct
chat the sender gets `message_read`; in a room the other members get
`room_read`.

200.description: What is left unread in this chat

put.description: Muted chats send no push. Messages still arrive on the socket.

until.description: A future time in unix seconds (INVALID_BODY otherwise). Leave out to mute until unmuted. Direct chats only.

get.description: Newest first unless `sort_dict` is `{"created_at": 1}`. Files of deleted messages are left out. No filter.

200.description: One page of files, or `{total_count}` with get_count

get.description: The records shared in this chat that you may open, newest first, at most 50 in all. No filter or sort.

200.description: One page of cards, or `{total_count}` with get_count

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The message id. In a direct chat, your copy's id, as history returns it.

patch.description: Your own messages only (`NOT_YOUR_MESSAGE`). The others get the edited frame.

delete.description:
Yours, or any message in a room you manage. The message stays as a stub with
`deleted: true`, its text, reactions and record removed, and replies quoting
it lose the quote. The file is deleted when it was the sender's own chat
upload and no other message uses it. The older read routes leave it out.

post.description:
One reaction per emoji per person; sending it again changes nothing. A message
takes at most 20 different emoji (`TOO_MANY_REACTIONS`). `INVALID_EMOJI`,
`MESSAGE_DELETED`.

Sends one message to one person. Form or query parameters.

To send a file, upload it first with `/messages/attachment_send`, then send
`att_id`, `att_path` (the returned `link`) and a `type` other than `text`.
With no `text`, the message reads "New <type> message".

The recipient gets a `message` socket frame and an `N010` push, unless they
muted you or are busy. A recipient who has been away for 20 minutes and
allows it gets an email. If the recipient set translation for you, their copy
holds the translated text and the original in `original_text`.

`version=3` sends the message to every admin of your tenant instead of
`to_id`; the response describes the last one.

Refusals: `INVALID_RECIPIENT`, `CANNOT_SEND_TO_SELF`,
`RECIPIENT_IS_A_COMPANY`, `YOU_ARE_IN_BLACKLIST` (they blocked you),
`ATTACHMENT_WAS_NOT_FOUND…`, and a limit of 5 unanswered messages to someone
who is not your contact.

quoted_text.description: Text of the message being replied to

user_message_type.description: `sms` also texts the recipient's phone from your softphone number.

get.description:
Your direct messages in both directions, newest first, with the people in
them. Pass `from` to read one chat.

With `from`, unread messages from that person are marked read as they are
returned, and the sender gets `message_read` frames. Send
`mark_as_read=false` to only look.

parameters.name: from_timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds; only messages after it

200.description: Messages and the people in them

client_users.description: People linked to a lead or contact (customers)

post.summary: Mark direct messages read or unread
post.description:
Changes your own copies only. Marking read tells the sender with a
`message_read` frame and updates the unread count for the pair. An id
that is not yours, or not found, is skipped.

msgid.description: One id or a comma-separated list

post.summary: Edit a direct message you sent
post.description:
Replaces the text of your message in both copies and sets `edited` to 1.
The recipient gets `message_edited`. The earlier text is not kept.
`msg_id` is accepted for `msgid`.

post.summary: Delete direct messages or clear a chat
post.description:
`msgid`: deletes messages you sent, both copies and the file. The recipient
gets `message_deleted`. `msg_id` is accepted for `msgid`.

`userid`: clears the chat with that person from your side only.

Send one of the two, or the answer is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`.

msgid.description: One id or a comma-separated list

userid.description: One person or a comma-separated list

post.description: Word search over your direct messages. Results carry a relevance `score`.

with_userid.description: Only the chat with this person

post.description:
People and rooms you have written with, newest message first. Each entry
says what it is in `conversation_with`: `user`, `client_user` or `room`.
People and rooms page separately, with `last_id_user` and `last_id_room`.
Reading the list does not mark anything read.

Uploads one file and answers its `att_id` and a signed `link`. Used for chat
and across the platform. HEIC photos are converted to JPEG, and large images
get a thumbnail. Counts against the tenant's storage.

Then send it: `att_id` + `att_path` on `/messages/send`, or `attachment_id` +
`att_path` on `/messages/send_room_message`.

get.summary: Read a file's details and link
get.description:
You may read a file you uploaded, a file in your tenant, a file sent to you
in a direct message, or a file posted in a room you are in. Any other id
answers `ATTACHMENT_WAS_NOT_FOUND…`, as an unknown id does.

get.summary: Read one room or list your rooms
get.description:
With `room_id`: that room, if you are a member (`NOT_ROOM_MEMBER…`
otherwise). Without it: the rooms you are in, newest first. `userid` narrows
the list to rooms you share with that person and returns at most one, which
is how a client finds its chat with a customer.

`match_filter_dict` is JSON with text filters `room_name` (or `name`),
`vanity_name` and `description` (contains, any case) and an exact
`room_type`. Other keys are ignored.

200.description: `room` is one Room with `room_id`, else a list

post.description:
JSON body. You become its admin. `user_ids` join as writers and get
`added_to_room` (send `do_notify: false` to skip that). A room name is unique
in the tenant: `ROOM_EXISTS_USE_PUT_TO_UPDATE`. Do not send `room_id`.

Only the fields listed are read. `virtual_phone` is kept only from a tenant
admin.

virtual_phone.description: The tenant number the room texts from

put.summary: Change a room or add members
put.description:
JSON body with `room_id`. Members may call it; every field change needs a
room admin or an admin of the room's tenant (`NOT_ROOM_ADMIN…`), and
`virtual_phone` needs the tenant admin. `user_ids` adds members, which also
needs an admin unless the room has `allow_self_add` and you add only
yourself. Members are changed through `user_ids`, `/room/remove` and
`/room/member/change_role`, never by sending `members`.

delete.description:
Deletes the room, its messages and files. A room admin or an admin of the
room's tenant may delete it, and a member with an individual account may
delete a client room. `msg` is `deleted` on success and says why otherwise.

parameters.name: delete_room_virtual_number
parameters.description: Also release the room's texting number

post.description:
The older form-parameter create. Same result as `POST /room/manage`.
`initial_members` is a comma-separated list of user ids.

post.summary: Every room you are in, with members
post.description: No parameters. Each room adds `room_avatar_url`, `is_admin` and member names, emails and avatars.

post.summary: Read a room, or change its name and settings
post.description:
With only `room_id`, any member reads the room with member details. Any
other field is a change and needs a room admin or an admin of the room's
tenant.

A room admin or an admin of the room's tenant adds anyone. In a room with
`allow_self_add`, a person in the room's tenant may add only themselves. Team rooms take staff
only; client and team rooms skip consumer accounts. Each new member gets
`added_to_room`, a push and an email.

post.summary: Leave a room, remove members, or delete rooms
post.description:
With `user_ids`: removes those members (room admin or admin of the room's
tenant). Each gets `removed_from_room` and an email.

Without `user_ids`: an admin deletes the rooms; anyone else leaves them,
where the room allows it.

Room admin or admin of the room's tenant. `new_role` is `0` writer, `1`
admin or `2` client. The last admin cannot be made a writer.
Refusals: `INVALID_ROLE`, `NOT_ROOM_MEMBER…`, `NOT_ROOM_ADMIN…`.
You may mute yourself. A room admin or an admin of the room's tenant may mute anyone.

post.summary: Invite people to a room by email
post.description:
JSON body. Room members only (`NOT_ROOM_MEMBER`). Each guest with a working
email address gets an invitation.

Members only (`NOT_ALLOWED_YOU_ARE_NOT_A_MEMBER…`). Every other member who
has not muted the room gets a `room_message` frame and an `N009` push.
`@name` and `@all` also email the people named.

A reply in a thread sets `parent_message_id` to the root message.

`user_message_type=sms` also texts every member's phone from the room's
number. Sending to a lead or contact by `prospect_id` creates their client
room on first use; that needs texting turned on for the tenant
(`NOT_TELCO_ENABLED`) and a softphone number for you
(`ENABLE_SIP_PHONE_FOR_USER`).

room_id.description: Required unless sending to a prospect

type.description: `0` text, `1` audio, `2` image, `3` video, `4` other file

initial_delay.description: Seconds to wait before the text goes out

post.description:
Top-level messages newest first, each with its thread replies under
`child_messages`. Pass `parent_message_id` to read one thread.

Reading the top level marks the returned messages read for you and moves
your read state, unless `mark_as_read=false`.

200.description: Messages and the people in them

post.description: `status=0` adds you to each message's `browsing` list and counts you in `browsing_cnt`.

The sender, a room admin or an admin of the room's tenant. Other members
get `room_message_edited`. `msg_id` is accepted for `msgid`.

post.summary: Delete a room message, or clear a room
post.description:
`msgid` (or `msg_id`): the sender, a room admin or an admin of the room's
tenant deletes the message and its file. Other members get
`room_message_deleted`.

`room_id`: deletes every message in the room. Room admin or admin of the
room's tenant only (`NOT_ROOM_ADMIN`).
Word search inside a room you are in. Results carry a relevance `score`.

get.description:
Contacts, friend requests and bots, with message counts per person.
`contact_type_filter=room` lists your rooms in the same shape.

parameters.name: friend
parameters.description: `1` contacts, `2` requests you sent, `3` requests you received

post.summary: Send or accept a contact request
Remove a contact or turn down a request

get.summary: Find a person by email or phone

post.description:
Confirmed people in your own tenant whose name, email or phone matches.
You are left out. This is the "New chat" people search.

post.summary: Find Ambivo users from a phone book
post.description:
JSON body. Send phone numbers, SHA-256 hashes of E.164 numbers, emails or
user ids; at most 200 results. Email and phone come back only for people in
your tenant. People who blocked you, or whom you blocked, are left out.
They can no longer send you direct messages. The encrypted service keeps its own list, `POST /v1/blocks`; apps set both.

post.summary: Get a token for the encrypted chat service
post.description:
Signed with Core's RS256 key, `aud` `ambivo-chat`, valid 3600 s. Claims:
`sub` (user id), `tenant_id`, `device_id`. Refusals: `MISSING_DEVICE_ID`
(400), `RS256_NOT_CONFIGURED` (503).

JSON body. One registration per user, tenant, device and app. Send it at
every sign-in; the token changes.

post.summary: Send a call signal to a person or a room
post.description:
JSON body. Relays a call frame (for example `video_voip`, `audio_voip`,
`video_hangup`, `audio_hangup`) over the socket, with a push. `to_roomid`
reaches every other member of a room you are in.

`to_userid` must be in your tenant or one of your contacts
(`RECIPIENT_NOT_ALLOWED`). `message_title` is cut to 200 characters and
`message_body` to 500.

The frame's `sender_id` is always you. Types the server sends itself
(`message`, `room_message`, `system_notification`, `send_device_sms` and the
other chat frames above) are not relayed.

Registers or replaces the key set of the device in your chat token. The
device id, user and tenant come from the token. A new device that has a
backup waiting is told with a `backup_available` frame.
Top up when `/v1/keys/count` runs low. The apps add 20 when fewer than 5 remain.

get.summary: One-time prekeys left on this device

get.description:
One bundle per active device of `user_id`, to start an encrypted session.
Only for yourself or someone you share a room with (403 `NO_SHARED_ROOM`), so
create the room first. Each call uses up one one-time prekey per device;
`one_time_prekey` is null when a device has none left. Devices unseen for 30
days are retired here.

Uses up no keys. An empty list means the person has no encrypted chat; the
apps then fall back to Core direct messages.

delete.description: It stops receiving messages. Call it at sign-out.

get.description: Every room you are in. No paging, no last message, no unread count.

post.description:
You become `admin`; others join as `member`. For a one-to-one chat the apps
first look for an existing `direct` room with exactly the two of you.

Being in a room with someone lets you fetch their keys, send to them and call
them, so creation is bounded: a `direct` room is you and one other person
(`DIRECT_NEEDS_ONE_PERSON`), a room has at most 256 people
(`TOO_MANY_MEMBERS`), and you can create at most 200 rooms a day (429
`ROOM_LIMIT_REACHED`).
`enc_metadata` is the room's name and description, encrypted by the client.

200.description: The room, at the top level
The room, at the top level

post.description:
Room admins only (403 `NOT_ROOM_ADMIN`). `role` is `member` or `admin`
(`INVALID_ROLE`). A direct room cannot grow (403 `ROOM_IS_DIRECT`). Members
must then send new sender keys, since the room's epoch moves on.

delete.description: You may remove yourself. Removing someone else takes a room admin (403 `NOT_ROOM_ADMIN`).

post.description:
One envelope per recipient device, each encrypted for that device. Include
your own other devices so they see what you sent. All envelopes share the
returned `message_id`.

Envelopes to someone not in the room, or to a device that is unknown, retired
or not that person's, are dropped. 403 `RECIPIENT_NOT_IN_ROOM` when nobody
addressed is in the room; `NO_VALID_RECIPIENTS` when nothing is left to send,
so refresh the recipient's devices with `/v1/keys/devices`. Envelopes to people who blocked you are dropped without saying so.
Each recipient device gets an `envelope` frame; devices that are offline get
a push. `msg_type` is the Signal message type: `3` for the first message of a
session, `2` after it, `7` for a group sender-key message.

content_hint.description: `text`, `media` or `control`. Tells push and the server what kind of message it is, never its content.

get.summary: This device's envelopes in a room
get.description:
Newest first. `last_id` is present only when the page is full; pass it as
`before` for the next page. Does not mark anything delivered. Most clients
use `/v1/sync` instead and keep history on the device.

Envelopes for this device after `since`, oldest first, across all rooms.
Returned envelopes count as delivered and their senders get receipts. Keep
the returned `last_id` and pass it as `since` next time; loop while a page
is full. Run it after every socket reconnect and on every chat push.

Most recent first. A message is `read` when every recipient device read it
and you share read receipts; otherwise at most `delivered`.

post.summary: Mark read up to an envelope
post.description: Same as the socket `read` frame. Nothing is recorded if you turned read receipts off.

Empties the ciphertext of every copy, so a device that has not synced never
gets it, and sends each recipient device a `deleted` frame. A device that
already decrypted it keeps its own copy until the app removes it.
`NOT_MESSAGE_OWNER` (403) for someone else's message.

post.summary: Hand out your group sender key
post.description: One encrypted copy per recipient device. Each gets a `senderkey` frame.

get.summary: Sender keys addressed to this device

post.summary: Get a link to upload an encrypted file
post.description:
Encrypt the file on the device, then `PUT` the ciphertext to `put_url` with
no auth header and no `Content-Type`. The link lasts an hour. The file key,
name and type travel inside the message.

get.summary: Get a link to download an encrypted file
get.description: `BLOB_NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id, `INVALID_ID` for a malformed one.

post.summary: Get a link to upload your chat backup
post.description: The backup is encrypted on the device with a passphrase the server never sees. One backup per person; a new one replaces it.

get.summary: Get a link to download your chat backup
get.description: HTTP 404 `NO_BACKUP` when there is none.

post.summary: Turn read receipts on or off
post.description: With it off, your reads are not recorded and you see no one else's.

get.description:
Title, description and image of a public web page, kept for 24 hours. A page
that cannot be read, or that redirects to a private address, answers with
nulls. `BAD_URL` (400) for a link that is
not http or https, `BLOCKED_HOST` (400) for a private address.

post.summary: Token for a voice or video call
post.description:
An Agora token for `channel`, valid an hour. A one-to-one call's channel is
`call_<lower user id>_<higher user id>`, and you get a token only for a
channel that names you (403 `CHANNEL_NOT_YOURS`). `AGORA_NOT_CONFIGURED`
(503) when calls are off.

post.summary: Register a push token with the chat service
post.description: Only used when the service sends push itself. In production Core sends it, so apps register with `POST /user/device_registrations/manage`.
`BAD_BOT_TOKEN` (400) when Telegram refuses the token, `WEBHOOK_FAILED` (502) when the webhook cannot be set.

get.summary: The link customers open to write to the bot
get.description: `NOT_CONNECTED` (404) with no bot.
Up to 200, newest first.
Up to 500. Reading clears the unread count. `NO_THREAD` (404).
